summary.en: を marks the thing directly acted upon—and is pronounced お in modern Japanese.

body.en:
From *ひだまり旅館*, season 1.

Because Japanese puts the verb at the very end of the clause, particles show what role each noun plays. The particle *を* (pronounced 'o') attaches right after the direct object—the thing you open, drink, check, or carry.

In *温かいお茶を飲んで* ('drink warm tea'), *お茶* is what you drink (*飲む*). In *このスーツケースの中を見てください* ('please look inside this suitcase'), *中* ('the inside') is what Kazuko asks Mio to look at (*見る*), and in *名札を確認しましょう* ('let us check the luggage tag'), *名札* is what gets checked.

The kana *を* appears almost exclusively as this particle in modern Japanese, making object boundaries easy to spot on the page.
